edit.description: Every row site in this file composes a host's address through `memberAddress` — `mentionRows` at 680, `includeRows` at 746, `inputRows` at 773, `nestedMemberRows`' `host` at 917, the placement/extent key at 838, `declaredAddresses` at 1149 — except the leaf branch at 693, which hands `embeddedLeafMentionRows` the bare `member.name`. It takes `memberAddress(member)` and the helper's `hostName` parameter (708) becomes the host's address. The defect the bare name leaves: since 00e61c77 a nested file child's `features.id` **is** its host-qualified address, so a leaf row headed `home/<kind>/<key>/<field>` matches no member at `read.rs`'s `resolve_leaf` (1510) and the leaf resolves nowhere — and two sibling children each named `home` head one string, the collision 1140's own comment ("two hosts may each carry a `home`, and a mention names one") names one grain up.

`leafAddress` (150) documents its `member` as carried verbatim "so a writer holding the bare member id spells the short form the lock already commits" — that justification is what this removes. The head is the host's own address at whatever grain the host sits: `kind:name` for a top-level host, the host's whole address under a nested one. The signature does not move; the contract its doc states does, and `isNameQualifier` (141) stays the guard that keeps the head one segment wide.

`resolve_leaf`'s head comment (1502) credits the bare-id branch (1510) to "the short form the lock already commits". With the SDK writing the canonical head at both grains that branch serves a **nested** host (whose `features.id` is its whole address) plus a lock written before this entry, which is what the comment should say; the `parse_host_address` branch (1511) carries the top-level case it used to share. Behaviour is unchanged — both spellings already resolve — and the in-file test lane (2812, 2887) gains the pin.

The file's addressing lane — 137's host-qualified target, 159's "never a leaf-scoped `<host>/<kind>/<key>` address" — gains the leaf row's own head, which nothing pins today (no test in `sdk/test/` reads a leaf mention row's `member` column). A top-level host's leaf row heads `kind:name`; a nested-file host's heads that host's whole address; two sibling children of one name head two distinct strings.

summary: A prose leaf's address heads with its host's own address, never the host's bare name — the one row site that joins locally reads `memberAddress` like its siblings

tests.asserts: a leaf mention row under a nested-file host heads that host's whole address, a top-level host's heads `kind:name`, and two sibling children of one name head two distinct strings
`resolve_leaf` resolves a leaf whose head is a nested host's own address, and still resolves a bare-id head

acceptance: `pnpm --dir sdk test` and `cargo test` green, with the leaf mention row's member column reading `memberAddress`'s spelling at both grains and a nested host's leaf resolving rather than naming no member.
notes: Swept out of the 13b3d9b5..HEAD window: e9c80335's body flagged this as out of its fence and no entry carried it. Blocked on both address readers — a leaf under a depth-1 host spells six segments, which `segment`'s `splitn(4, '/')` cannot read, and `memberAddress`'s own head is only right at depth 2 once the SDK parity entry lands.
